candidates.non_vesting_text: By the President of the United States of America  A Proclamation  MODIFYING [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], AS AMENDED, RELATING TO IMPORTS OF PETROLEUM AND PETROLEUM PRODUCTS, AND PROVIDING FOR THE LONG-TERM CONTROL OF IMPORTS OF PETROLEUM AND PETROLEUM PRODUCTS THROUGH A SYSTEM OF LICENSE FEES  Whereas, I judge it necessary and consistent with the national security, taking into account the economic welfare of the Nation, that provision be made to defer scheduled increases in the fees applicable to imported petroleum and petroleum products for a period of two months; and  Whereas, it is my intention that refiners located in territories of the United States, and in foreign trade zones, shall participate in the Mandatory Oil Import Program upon terms not less favorable than domestic refiners; and  Whereas, in order to facilitate such treatment, it is necessary that the Administrator of the Federal Energy Administration be authorized to determine at what point the oil import license fees effective February 1, 1975 shall be deemed to apply with respect to crude oil entered into such territories and zones; and  Whereas, I judge it necessary to permit a system for the receipt by Puerto Rico of sums equivalent to the license fees on petroleum consumed in Puerto Rico, to be appropriated by the Commonwealth for the benefit of individuals and corporations resident therein, comparable to the system which I have proposed for other parts of the United States;  Now, Therefore, I, Gerald R. Ford, President of the United States of America, acting [VESTING_CLAUSE_REMOVED] do hereby proclaim that, effective as of February 1, 1975, [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE], as amended, is hereby further amended as follows :  SECTION 1. Subparagraphs (iii), (iv), and (viii) of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (a) of section 3 are amended to read as follows:  "(iii) with respect to imports of crude oil, natural gas products, unfinished oils, and all other finished products (except ethane, propane, butanes, and asphalt) entered into the customs territory of the United States on or after February 1, 1975, there shall be a supplemental fee per barrel of $1.00, rising to $2.00 on imports entered on or after May 1, 1975, and to $3.00 on imports entered on or after June 1, 1975;  (iv) with respect to the fees imposed pursuant to paragraphs 3(a)(1)(i)-(iii), the amount of such fees shall be reduced, on a monthly basis, by an amount equal to any applicable duties paid less any drawbacks received during the same period, except that where duty drawbacks exceed the duty paid during that period, the net differences shall be applied to subsequent periods; provided that when the duty less drawbacks exceeds the fee imposed, the Administrator may provide that any excess may be used to reduce fees payable in subsequent months, such extended period not to exceed six months;  (viii) with respect to licenses issued pursuant to paragraph 3 (a) (1) (iii) for imports other than (A) crude oil as defined for purposes of the Old Oil Allocation Program which is imported for refining or (B) products refined in a refinery outside of the customs territory as to which crude oil runs to stills would qualify a refiner to receive entitlements under the Old Oil Allocation Program, the Administrator may by regulation reduce the fee payable by the following amounts, or by such other amounts as he may determine to be necessary to achieve the objectives of this Proclamation and the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973:  -for imports entered into the United States customs territory during the months of February, March and April, 1975, $1.00 per barrel;  -for imports entered during the month of May, 1975, $1.40 per barrel;  -for imports entered during the month of June, 1975, and thereafter, $1.80 per barrel."  SECTION 2. Paragraph (a) of Section 3 is amended by adding subparagraph (5) to read as follows :  " (5) In order to ensure that refiners located in territories of the United States and in foreign trade zones are treated not less favorably than other United States refiners, the Administrator shall by regulation determine at what point crude oil, unfinished oils and finished products shipped into United States territories and foreign trade zones shall become subject to the fees imposed pursuant to paragraphs 3 (a) (1) (i) - (iii)."  SECTION 3. Subparagraph (1) of paragraph (a) of Section 3 is amended by adding clause (x) to read as follows:  "(x) The Administrator shall by regulation reduce the fees payable by importers pursuant to paragraphs 3 (a) (1) (i) - (iii) with respect to crude oil, unfinished oils, and finished products imported into Puerto Rico, or imported into Districts I-V and shipped to Puerto Rico, with or without further processing, and not shipped to Districts I-V, as crude oil, unfinished oils, or finished products, by the amount of any excise tax or other levy imposed and collected by the Government of Puerto Rico on such materials, Provided that refunds from or reductions in such excise tax or other levy are authorized in the same manner as are authorized with respect to payments prescribed by paragraphs 3 (a) (1) (i)-(iii), Provided further that with respect to shipments to Puerto Rico from Districts I-V such shipments shall be deemed attributable to imported crude."  In Witness Whereof, I have hereunto set my hand this fourth day of March, in the year of our Lord nineteen hundred seventy-five, and of the Independence of the United States of America the one hundred and ninety-ninth.  GERALD R. FORD

policy_functions.mechanism: imposing supplemental fees per barrel, providing for duty offset reductions, and authorizing administrative fee reductions
policy_functions.effect: modifies license fees on crude oil, natural gas products, unfinished oils, and finished products entered into the U.S. customs territory

policy_functions.label: Equalize treatment for refiners in territories and foreign trade zones
policy_functions.actor: Administrator of the Federal Energy Administration
policy_functions.target: crude oil, unfinished oils, and finished products shipped into U.S. territories and foreign trade zones
policy_functions.mechanism: issuing regulations to define when fee obligations attach
policy_functions.effect: ensures refiners in territories and foreign trade zones participate on terms not less favorable than domestic refiners

policy_functions.label: Provide fee reductions for imports into Puerto Rico equivalent to local excise taxes
policy_functions.actor: Administrator of the Federal Energy Administration
policy_functions.target: crude oil, unfinished oils, and finished products imported into or shipped to Puerto Rico
policy_functions.mechanism: issuing regulations reducing import fees by the amount of excise tax or other levy imposed and collected by the Government of Puerto Rico
policy_functions.effect: establishes a system comparable to other parts of the U.S. for Puerto Rico to receive equivalent sums from petroleum import fees
policy_functions.condition: provided that refunds or reductions in Puerto Rico's excise tax/levy are authorized in the same manner as prescribed fee payments, and shipments from Districts I-V are deemed attributable to imported crude

operative_functions.label: Establish effective date of proclamation amendments
operative_functions.target: oil import authority regulations
operative_functions.mechanism: prescribing effective date
operative_functions.effect: makes amendments retroactively effective as of February 1, 1975
operative_functions.timing: effective as of February 1, 1975

operative_functions.label: Impose supplemental per-barrel import fees on petroleum and products
operative_functions.action: amend section 3(a)(1)(iii) to impose supplemental fee schedule
operative_functions.target: imports of crude oil, natural gas products, unfinished oils, and finished products (except ethane, propane, butanes, and asphalt)
operative_functions.mechanism: establishing supplemental fee per barrel rising from $1.00 to $2.00 and $3.00
operative_functions.effect: increases fees on petroleum imports entered into U.S. customs territory
operative_functions.timing: entered on or after February 1, 1975 ($1.00), May 1, 1975 ($2.00), and June 1, 1975 ($3.00)

operative_functions.label: Reduce import fees by duties paid less drawbacks
operative_functions.action: reduce fees monthly and carry forward excess drawbacks or duty credits
operative_functions.target: fees imposed pursuant to paragraphs 3(a)(1)(i)-(iii)
operative_functions.mechanism: offsetting fees by applicable duties paid less drawbacks, carrying forward net differences or excess duty offset up to six months
operative_functions.effect: prevents double-taxation of imports subject to both customs duties and license fees
operative_functions.condition: where duty drawbacks exceed duty paid, or where duty less drawbacks exceeds the fee imposed
operative_functions.timing: monthly basis; extended period not to exceed six months

operative_functions.label: Empower Administrator to reduce fees for specified non-entitlement imports
operative_functions.target: licenses for imports other than crude oil imported for refining or products qualifying for entitlements under the Old Oil Allocation Program
operative_functions.mechanism: issuing regulations reducing fees by specified schedule or other amounts necessary to achieve proclamation objectives
operative_functions.effect: provides discretionary fee reductions for non-entitlement petroleum imports
operative_functions.timing: February-April 1975 ($1.00/bbl), May 1975 ($1.40/bbl), June 1975 and thereafter ($1.80/bbl)

operative_functions.label: Direct Administrator to establish point of fee applicability for territories and FTZs
operative_functions.action: determine point of fee applicability by regulation
operative_functions.target: crude oil, unfinished oils, and finished products shipped into U.S. territories and foreign trade zones
operative_functions.mechanism: promulgating regulations defining when shipments become subject to fees
operative_functions.effect: ensures equal treatment for territorial and foreign trade zone refiners relative to other U.S. refiners

operative_functions.label: Direct Administrator to reduce fees on imports into Puerto Rico by local tax amounts
operative_functions.action: reduce fees payable by importers by regulation
operative_functions.target: crude oil, unfinished oils, and finished products imported into or shipped to Puerto Rico
operative_functions.mechanism: deducting excise tax or other levy amounts imposed and collected by the Government of Puerto Rico
operative_functions.effect: offsets federal import fees by local Puerto Rican taxes levied on the materials
operative_functions.condition: provided that refunds or reductions in local tax are authorized in the same manner as fee payments, and shipments from Districts I-V are deemed attributable to imported crude
